messages.subject: Rattle 2.6.11 Released
parts:
Rattle 2.6.11 is now on the master CRAN node and is propagating.

Start up R and:

> library(rattle)
> install.packages(rattleInfo())

The main update is a fix for those using Mac OS/X (a version number bug).

There is also some minor internal code cleanup.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Rattle 2.6.11 Released
parts: On 20 January 2012 07:34, Paul <paul...@ecolab.com> wrote:
Hello,  I've tried to update rattle using the instructions below.  I've attached much of the output in teh RGUI wondow, and it probably pegs my efforts as confused, at best.
Hi Paul,

> library(rattle)
> install.packages(rattleInfo())
 
 
Questions:
1)  Warning: package ‘rattle’ is in use and will not be installed
-- it seems that rattle is immediately attached when I start the RGUI, and must be detached to install rattle?
> detach("package:rattle")

Oops - I overlooked that issue - I'll have to do something special to upgrade rattle in this way. 

Also, rattle should only be attached after a library("rattle") call, not automatically every time you start RGui? One of the messages below (which is followed by a rattle time stamp and then followed by you loading rattle into the library) would suggest that somehow rattle has left some traces in your workspace - did you save your workspace from a previous R - might be best to rename the .RData file in the current folder to .RData.old to test that "immediately attached" issue.

2) Does the installation want me to choose the dependent packages for updating?  Why does does the packages dialog box appear with the entire list of R's packages?
 
Installed Dependencies
pmml: version 1.2.28
colorspace: version 1.1-1
 
ETC.
 
rpart: version 3.1-51
survival: version 2.36-10

That was 30 packages.
Not quite sure what you mean by a dialog box - rattleInfo() lists version numbers of installed dependent packages and whether there is an update available.

3) RGtk2 is at the center of error messages that I cannot make sense of, although I 've read througha number of help messages. Do I get "Warning: cannot remove prior installation of package ‘RGtk2’" because Windows 7 is so strict about administrative rights to install/remove/modify files that appear executable?

Try doing this without involving rattle to avoid any potential confusion. Start up a vanilla R and then try install.packages("RGtk2"). The message could indicate that you installed RGtk2 as an administrator on Windows 7 but are now trying to install it into the same location as a user - though R would normally try to install it into your local folder if you are not an administrator, and the messages below indicate this is the case (local user folder). Try manually removing  C:/Users/prewpj/Documents/R/win-library/2.14/RGtk2 and then installing RGtk2 from inside R.
 
[...]

2.       To edit data on-screen with a GUI is quite a nice feature – must I use the Execute button to have changes take effect on the underlying RData file?  Is it possible to make such edits using the View button, or does the Edit button always ne dot be chosen?

Screenshot below shows the 2nd radio button selected for Prod.Pref., meaning that it is the target variable, with class = Numeric.  However, this target variable is truly Categoric with the unfortunate categories of [1,2], leading rattle to interpret as numeric upon loading.  I should have changed it to a [One, Two] using Excel before importing with rattle.  Instead, I had changed the class to Character last week using rattle’s Edit function, which is why I believe the status bar says Prod.Pref is Categoric.

 

 

 

It appears that rattle is interpreting the column as a Numeric target, not Categoric.   Using the Data tab > Edit, and right-clicking on the Prod.Pref column header, it shows that rattle interprets the Prod.Pref. column as Integer.

Thanks, Paul

Maybe not - rattleInfo() is returning a list of packages to install. If none need updating then an empty list is passed to install.packages() which will ask you for packages that you want installed.

2.       To edit data on-screen with a GUI is quite a nice feature – must I use the Execute button to have changes take effect on the underlying RData file?  Is it possible to make such edits using the View button, or does the Edit button always ne dot be chosen?
View will not change the data. After Edit you need to select the R Dataset that is named in the message, then Execute

3.      Conflicting information on class of target variable

Screenshot below shows the 2nd radio button selected for Prod.Pref., meaning that it is the target variable, with class = Numeric.  However, this target variable is truly Categoric with the unfortunate categories of [1,2], leading rattle to interpret as numeric upon loading.  I should have changed it to a [One, Two] using Excel before importing with rattle.  Instead, I had changed the class to Character last week using rattle’s Edit function, which is why I believe the status bar says Prod.Pref is Categoric.

 

 

 

It appears that rattle is interpreting the column as a Numeric target, not Categoric.   Using the Data tab > Edit, and right-clicking on the Prod.Pref column header, it shows that rattle interprets the Prod.Pref. column as Integer.

Thanks Paul - that looks like a bug - I'll have a look. Rattle tries to use some heuristics to decide on the target types - probably getting something wrong there.

Regards,
Graham
